The blades are among the most expensive components of a wind turbine, accounting for 10-20% of total manufacturing costs.
Larger and more flexible blades have been designed to harvest more energy, but this has led to lower safety margins.
Cracks and delaminations are the most common forms of damage in wind turbine blades, typically occurring close to the blade root.
Damage in wind turbine blades can lead to critical failures that can damage not only the turbine they are attached to, but also other nearby turbines.
The proposed SHM system uses SCADA data, which has a low-pass filter applied and is logged at 10-minute intervals.
The GPs are trained on 2500 randomly selected data points from the first 2 years of turbine operation.
The GPs use a combination of squared-exponential and Bayesian linear covariance functions.
The hyperparameters of the GPs are learned by maximizing the log marginal likelihood using the Nelder-Mead optimization algorithm.
The X-bar control charts use 3σ thresholds calculated over a 6-month period after the initial GP training.
The case studies showed the proposed SHM system could identify early onset of damage up to 6 months before it was identified through traditional inspection methods.
The proposed SHM system can help minimize downtime, maximize reliability, reduce operation and maintenance costs, and extend the design lifetime of wind turbine blades.

By analyzing the relative relationships between the edge frequencies of the three blades, the complex nonstationarities due to environmental and operational variables are transformed into a simpler, more explicable space.
GPs are more robust to the nonlinear and noisy relationships between the edge frequencies and environmental/operational variables, as the functional forms do not need to be predetermined.
The use of X-bar control charts with 3σ thresholds allows the SHM system to balance the trade-off between true and false positives in damage detection.
The versatility of the proposed methodology means it can also be applied to offshore wind turbines.
